thesis: His four book recommendations connect constraints, subtraction, identity and detachment from outcomes.
summary: Martell favors just-in-time study with learn/do/teach. His reading of The Goal identifies and stabilizes a bottleneck; The Effective Executive supports time auditing and abandonment; Feeling Is the Secret supplies assumed-identity and visualization exercises; Inner Excellence shifts attention from gripping outcomes to prepared, present performance. He offers concrete flow-mapping, calendar and pre-performance exercises.

review_status: Codex editorial draft; complete local transcript read; claims not independently verified
synthesis_method: Direct Codex extraction from complete local transcript; exact quotations verified locally
context_and_limits: These are Martell’s interpretations, not a review of the books themselves. Author names are imperfectly transcribed; titles identify the works without claiming all quoted passages were checked against editions. Wealth/reading totals, celebrity stories and exact productivity shares are unverified. Goddard’s thought-to-outcome claims are belief, not demonstrated causality. Just-in-time business study differs from a universal judgment against leisure reading.
review_changes: Restores the substantial Goddard identity/manifestation section and its evidentiary status, plus the complementary input-control versus outcome-attachment lesson.
